summary: This House resolution recognizes the 50th anniversary of Cabo Verde's 1975 independence from Portugal, commends its democratic governance and support for Ukraine, and highlights the historical ties and ongoing contributions of Cabo Verdean-Americans to both nations.

scores.thoughts: The resolution is purely symbolic and commemorative. It contains no provisions authorizing, expanding, or reducing any government expenditures or programs.
No references to tax policy, rates, or reforms appear in the text.
A single clause notes Cabo Verde's malaria-free declaration and general U.S.-supported health initiatives, but this is historical background only and does not alter U.S. healthcare policy.
The bill has no connection to firearms regulation or Second Amendment issues.
Historical emigration from Cabo Verde and the contributions of Cabo Verdean-Americans are acknowledged, yet the resolution enacts no changes to immigration law or policy.
No content relates to reproductive rights or abortion access.
Mentions of National Guard partnership exercises and bilateral military cooperation are factual background only; the resolution does not alter defense spending or posture.
A brief reference to a 'Blue-Green Futures' delegation on sustainable marine research exists but is incidental and does not modify environmental regulations.
No provisions address welfare programs, food assistance, or related entitlements.
An academic institute is mentioned in passing; the resolution creates no education policy or funding changes.
The bill is silent on drug enforcement or decriminalization.
No references to sentencing, policing, or justice reform.
Historical trade routes are noted but the resolution does not establish or modify trade policy.
No fiscal or debt-related provisions are present.
The resolution contains no language concerning LGBTQ+ legal protections.
Past Millennium Challenge Corporation compacts and Peace Corps involvement are cited as historical facts; the resolution neither authorizes new aid nor calls for reductions.
Democratic multiparty elections in Cabo Verde are praised, but this is descriptive only and does not affect U.S. voting or election laws.
No provisions relate to technology regulation or data privacy.
Historical labor contributions of Cabo Verdean-Americans are mentioned without any policy implications for unions or workers' rights.
The bill does not address religious exemptions or anti-discrimination law.
